description: The hand-verified expected result for the captured Joern fixture. Every value was derived by reading fixtures/joern.json and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, and every path was resolved by a second resolver written from the documented indexing scheme alone rather than by importing normalize.paths. The adapter was run only afterwards, to corroborate. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
scanner_class_authority: AAP 0.5.4's class table fixes sast for opengrep, semgrep, datadog-static-analyzer and joern. joern is the one of the four that writes a native shape, so it is the only one of them with its own adapter. The value is fixed in advance rather than derived from what the artifact turns out to contain, and it is identical on every row.
artifact_shape_note: This is the only artifact whose shape is the harness's own collector output rather than a tool-native format. There is no Joern output format to look up: harness/bin/run-joern.sh loads the graph with importCpg, runs the bounded query set baked into harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, and that script writes the artifact itself.

fixture.provenance: CAPTURED. Every one of the fourteen findings is a whole element of harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json's findings array, copied out verbatim in raw document order, and every envelope member -- tool, tool_version, cpg, graph, query_set and the entire queries array -- is the raw artifact's byte for byte. Nothing in this fixture was authored, re-spelled or adjusted. AAP 0.6.2 gives the reason: a hand-written fixture tests the adapter against the shape you believed the tool emits rather than the shape it emits.
fixture.capture_method: The raw artifact writes one finding per physical line. The fourteen lines at the indexes above were taken unchanged, in the order they appear, and the envelope lines preceding the findings array were copied unchanged. Only the trailing comma of the last selected line was dropped, so that the excerpt is a valid JSON document.
fixture.capture_verification: RawArtifactProvenanceTest in test_joern_adapter.py opens the raw artifact and asserts each selected finding is identical to the raw object under canonical comparison -- json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True) -- in raw document order, that every envelope member equals the raw artifact's, and that the fixture introduces no member the raw artifact lacks. The digest above is checked against the file rather than against another copy of itself.
fixture.why_these_fourteen: The selection covers both outcomes the raw artifact really produces and all six of its query identifiers. Eleven findings name a class that resolves uniquely to one src/main source file and become rows -- nine in scope and two outside the twelve globs -- and three name a third-party class shaded into Spark's JARs, which resolves to nothing and is a counted unresolvable_path rejection. Three of the eleven resolve on the declaration scheme alone. That mix is the artifact's own: over all 692 findings, 107 resolve and 585 do not.
fixture.what_a_capture_of_this_artifact_cannot_s: A finding resolving into a src/test tree. See aap_requirement_coverage below: the raw artifact carries no test-tree class at all, so the requirement is exercised on the explicitly derived fixture rather than claimed here.
fixture.excerpt_note: The fixture is never edited to suit these rows; these rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible.

captured_positive_mapping.requirement: AAP 0.6.2 and 0.9.4: an unmodified captured fixture per adapter for positive mapping, with a hand-verified expected result asserted field by field.
captured_positive_mapping.evidence: The fixture is a verbatim excerpt of the tool's own artifact and it produces eleven rows, each asserted field by field over emit.FIELDS.

src_test_resolution_retained.requirement: AAP 0.5.4 and 0.6.1: a finding resolving into a src/test tree is RETAINED with in_scope false rather than dropped, and AAP 0.9.3 lists that retention among the conditions that are recorded and do not stop the run.
src_test_resolution_retained.status: COVERED ON A DECLARED-DERIVED FIXTURE, NOT ON THIS CAPTURE
src_test_resolution_retained.statement: This captured fixture cannot exercise the requirement, because the artifact it is an excerpt of contains no test-tree class to capture. The requirement is not waived and it is not treated as inapplicable: it is exercised on oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-joern-features.json, which declares itself derived and exists for exactly this case. Recording the case against a captured fixture by authoring a record into it would have made the capture claim false, which is the trade AAP 0.6.2 forbids.

measured_evidence.why: The runbook excludes every -tests JAR from the graph input, so no test-tree class reached the graph this artifact was queried from.
measured_evidence.asserted_by: RawArtifactProvenanceTest.test_the_raw_artifact_carries_no_test_tree_class in test_joern_adapter.py, so this is a measured claim rather than a statement in prose.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py restates as its own FIELDS because AAP 0.6.4 permits an adapter to import paths and severity and nothing else. The two were compared and are identical. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent. path in particular is not an optional field (AAP 0.5.4), so a record whose coordinate cannot be resolved is a counted rejection rather than a row with a null path.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched, or the reason it matched none, is recorded per row under row_derivations.

shape_divergence.summary: The artifact this fixture captures is written in this provisioning's collector shape, which differs from the collector shape the specification documents. The divergence is recorded, not repaired -- AAP 0.1.3's authority rule -- and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py reads both shapes for exactly that reason, in a fixed field precedence so the choice is reproducible. Three members differ, and each changes a value in the rows below.
shape_divergence.documented_shape: {tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size, queries: [{id, count}], findings: [{rule_id, message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file, path_resolution}]}
shape_divergence.provisioned_shape: {tool, tool_version, cpg, graph: {methods, type_declarations, files}, query_set, queries: [{id, bound, returned, bound_reached, elapsed_ms, callee_prefixes[]}], findings: [{query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file, line}]}

differences.documented: findings[].rule_id, one of five joern.-prefixed literals
differences.observed: findings[].query_id, one of the six identifiers harness/lib/joern-scan.sc bakes
differences.consequence: Every rule_id below is a joern- prefixed identifier rather than a joern. prefixed one, read from RULE_ID_FIELDS = ('rule_id', 'query_id') in that precedence. The counter reads 14 rather than 11, because the rule identifier is read at step 2 and the three rejections happen at step 4: a counter that only reached the rows would hide the order the classification runs in. rule_id_from_rule_id counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_not_a_guess: The prohibition on taking a rule_id from a queries[].id exists because the documented shape's queries[] carries only {id, count} and records no link between a query and a finding, so any match there would be inference. In this shape each finding carries its own query_id member, so the record itself names the query that produced it and nothing is inferred. KNOWN_RULE_IDS in the adapter carries both vocabularies -- this provisioning's six and the documented five -- and is explicitly never used to filter, because AAP 0.4.2 has the baked query set read from the runner rather than assumed.

differences.documented: no severity member at all, so severity_native null and severity_norm Info on every row
differences.observed: findings[].severity, HIGH or MEDIUM on every record
differences.consequence: Every row below carries severity_native HIGH or MEDIUM and severity_norm High or Medium, with basis label. severity_from_record_label counts 11 -- the tally is fed once per emitted row, never per record -- and severity_absent counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_the_contract: AAP 0.5.4 places joern under 'No vocabulary at all (gitleaks; joern unless a query defines one)'. Here a query does define one: all six baked queries declare a severity. The no-vocabulary path -- severity_native null with severity_norm Info and the absence stated rather than a level assumed -- is implemented and remains the behaviour for a record carrying no label, and it is simply not the path this artifact takes. Nothing is hard-coded either way: severity.py owns the vocabulary, so this file cannot disagree with severity-map.md.
differences.corroboration: All 107 joern rows in the committed oss-scan-results/findings.json carry severity_native HIGH or MEDIUM. None carries null.

differences.documented: flat cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size
differences.observed: a nested graph object carrying methods, type_declarations and files
differences.consequence: envelope_graph_methods, envelope_graph_type_declarations and envelope_graph_files carry the graph's figures, while envelope_collector_source_index_size and envelope_collector_declaration_index_size stay 0 because the flat members are absent. The per-query tally is spelled returned here rather than count, and neither is summed into any published figure.

shape_divergence.path_resolution_member: Absent from this fixture entirely: this provisioning's collector emits no path_resolution, so collector_explanation_present is 0. The rule it is subject to is unchanged and is structural rather than conditional -- AAP 0.5.4 has any collector explanation for an unmappable bytecode path retained in the rejection record and in no dataset field, and a twelve-key row has nowhere to put one. paths.resolve_bytecode_class composes it on every rejection route it can take, including the absent, blank and non-string identifier routes, and returns the detail unchanged where none was supplied -- which is why the three rejection details below carry no suffix. The same holds for the documented findings[].path member, which this fixture also does not carry, so collector_path_refused, collector_path_corroborated and collector_path_disagreed are all 0.
shape_divergence.file_member: Every record carries a file member holding the frontend's ephemeral extraction path. It is never read as a path. harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json names it record_path_field_to_ignore for exactly this reason, and the class member -- named record_path_field -- is the only resolvable coordinate.

count_unit.per_query_tally_member: queries[].returned in this shape; queries[].count in the documented shape
count_unit.which_one_is_the_raw_count: len(findings) = 14. The sum of the per-query tallies is 692 and is not the raw count and is not published as one.
count_unit.why_they_differ: The fixture excerpts 14 of the raw artifact's 692 findings while carrying the raw artifact's queries[] array unchanged. The two numbers therefore differ by construction, which is what makes the reconciliation assertion non-vacuous: an implementation that counted the per-query tallies instead of the findings would produce 692 against 11 rows and 3 rejections and fail rather than silently agree.
count_unit.authority: AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, and normalize.reconcile.count_records walks that same unit without building rows. The adapter deliberately publishes no count of the findings it walked, so that the left-hand side of the identity cannot be taken from the traversal that builds the right-hand side.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of findings[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.one_finding_one_outcome: Structural rather than asserted: the adapter's per-finding function returns a single value that is either a row or a rejection, so there is no path that emits both and none that emits neither.
counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = "partial", assigned where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the three rejected records are counted under their class with their reason retained. A capture of this artifact cannot be clean -- most of what the tool reported names a shaded third-party class -- and the fixture that is clean is the derived one.
counts.not_applicable_is_a_different_case: An artifact that was never written reconciles as not applicable -- artifact absent, not as zero equals zero. That case belongs to osv-scanner, which wrote nothing, and it is not this fixture's.
counts.note: Three of the fourteen classes are third-party classes shaded into Spark's JARs, which no source file in either tree declares, so each is a counted unresolvable_path rejection rather than a row with an invented path. This is the ordinary outcome for this artifact rather than a rare one: over all 692 findings, 585 resolve to nothing. The ambiguous case -- a class key two source files claim -- is not present here and is covered by reject-joern-ambiguous-path.json.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): 43 keys -- 23 authored, 5 envelope integers, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member, one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member, and one provenance key per member of each field-candidate tuple. The keys above are in COUNTER_KEYS order and the set is complete: every key the adapter initialises appears, so a zero here means measured-zero rather than not-measured.
counters_note: Four groups deserve reading together. The row decomposition rows_in_scope 9 + rows_out_of_scope 2 sums to the row count, because it is one measurement split rather than a second count of the same thing. The two step-2 and step-4 provenance counters -- rule_id_from_query_id and coordinate_from_class -- read 14 rather than 11, because the rule identifier and the coordinate field are read before the resolution that rejects three records; a reader comparing them with the row count is seeing the classification order rather than a discrepancy. The six source_index_* keys describe the index the resolution ran against rather than the records, and they are the figures that make a rejection count interpretable -- source_index_supplied 0 records that the adapter built the index over the pinned root rather than being handed one, so a test injecting a synthetic index through SourceIndex.from_mapping changes exactly these keys and nothing else. The five envelope_* graph keys are metadata for tool-status.md and contribute nothing to any record count.

aap_reported_counters.note: AAP 0.5.4 has four counters reported per tool. Two are members of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS and two are not, and the reason the two are absent is structural rather than an omission.

multi_location_records.basis: No finding in this shape carries a locations array; each names exactly one call site through its class, method and line members. The counter is published anyway, so that a future collector emitting several locations is visible rather than silently reduced to its first.

non_filesystem_paths.basis: Every path below has kind bytecode_source, which normalize.paths.is_non_filesystem_kind excludes -- only outside_root and archive_member are non-filesystem coordinates. Each resolved path names a real file in the pinned tree. The three rejected records produced no path at all, so they contribute to no path_kind_* counter and to this one not at all.

multi_valued_cwe_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS; the SARIF adapter publishes it because a SARIF rule can carry several CWE tokens. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a weakness catalogue entry, so cwe is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0. Manufacturing a CWE from a class name or a query identifier would be inference.

multi_valued_cve_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS, for the same reason: this shape carries no advisory identifier, so cve is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0.

envelope_fields.note: The envelope members outside findings[] are not findings and produce no rows. They must not appear in any row, and a twelve-key row makes that structural. They are recorded here because build-record.md and run-record.md cross-reference the graph figures, and a number that reaches no channel reaches no document.

documented_members_absent.cpg_methods: absent -- the figure arrives as graph.methods instead, and the counter envelope_graph_methods carries it
documented_members_absent.cpg_typedecls: absent -- the figure arrives as graph.type_declarations instead, and the counter envelope_graph_type_declarations carries it

envelope_fields.cpg_member: The envelope also carries a cpg member naming the graph file. It is an absolute path in the artifact and is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths; the graph's identity is recorded in run-record.md by byte size and sha256.
envelope_fields.bound_reached: No query reports reaching its traversal bound, so no per-query result below is truncated. Truncation is read from the flag rather than assumed, because a truncated query's silence would otherwise be indistinguishable from a clean one.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the joern entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_no_filesystem_base_exists: The runner queries a graph the frontend built over staged JARs rather than over the source tree, so the emitted file member is by construction the frontend's extraction path for a .class member and can never be a path in the Spark tree. The metadata therefore records a null base value rather than inventing a plausible one, and the class member is the only resolvable coordinate.
resolution_context.resolution_procedure: The class member -- a dotted type full name -- is reduced by normalize.paths.class_key to <package path>/<outer type name>, truncating the basename at its first $ so a companion object, an anonymous class and a nested class all collapse to the outer type. That key is then looked up in a source index over src/main and src/test under the pinned root, across two key schemes: by_filename on <package dir>/<file base name>, and by_decl on <package dir>/<declared type name>. The union of candidates must be exactly one distinct path.
resolution_context.gap_1_closed: The index spans src/main and src/test rather than src/main alone. Every -tests artifact the build emitted is in the graph input, so a finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree. No finding in this artifact does -- see aap_requirement_coverage -- so the retained src/test row is asserted on the derived fixture, and every one of the eleven rows here resolves into src/main.
resolution_context.gap_2_closed: A resolution is taken only where the union of candidates is exactly one distinct path. Two or more is ambiguous_source_resolution with every competing candidate named, never a first-wins pick. Closing gap 1 increases ambiguity, which is why closing gap 2 is mandatory rather than optional.
resolution_context.declaration_scheme_is_not_optional: Three of the eleven rows resolve on the declaration scheme alone -- ProcessBuilderLike is declared in DriverRunner.scala, RangePartitioner in Partitioner.scala and ObjectInputStreamWithLoader in Checkpoint.scala. A filename-only index would lose all three silently, and a silently lost row is indistinguishable from a class with nothing to report.
resolution_context.root_dependence: Unlike the SARIF fixtures, these rows depend on a live tree: the class-to-source resolution reads the pinned checkout at $SPARK_SRC. Every emitted path is expressed relative to that root and none is absolute. The index figures under counters are the measurement over the pinned tree, and they reproduce the figures the adapter's own docstring records.
resolution_context.severity_source: Every record states its own severity label, so severity_native is that literal verbatim and severity_norm comes from severity.py's label table: HIGH High, MEDIUM Medium. The label governs whenever it is in the mapped vocabulary and no score is consulted, which is the label-over-score precedence severity-map.md states.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. The absence is explicitly not a rejection: the unformable_package_coordinate class covers a dependency-oriented record, and this shape is not one.
resolution_context.unresolvable_is_the_common_outcome: Resolution failing is not an edge case for this artifact. The graph was built over every JAR the build produced, so most of what the queries matched is a third-party class shaded under the org.sparkproject prefix or a dependency on the classpath: 585 of the 692 findings resolve to nothing and are counted rejections. Three of them are in this fixture, so the capture exercises the rejection route on the tool's own records rather than only on a derived one.

independent_resolver.method: Every path below was first resolved by a second resolver written from the documented indexing scheme alone, which does not import normalize.paths. It reproduced the adapter's own recorded index measurements exactly over the pinned checkout: 6759 files indexed, 6755 by_filename keys of which 4 are ambiguous, and 15230 by_decl keys of which 107 are ambiguous.
independent_resolver.outcome_over_the_whole_raw_artifact: The same resolver run over all 692 raw findings resolves 107 uniquely, resolves 0 ambiguously and fails on 585 -- which is why the committed dataset carries exactly 107 joern rows.

adapter_run.when: after the hand derivation, never before it
adapter_run.note: Running the adapter over the fixture with the recorded runner metadata and a scaffold root reproduces all twelve fields of all eleven rows, all three rejections and all 43 counter values. That is corroboration recorded after the fact, not the source of these values.

committed_dataset.note: Each of the eleven rows below appears in the committed dataset with its rule_id, path, start_line, severity_native, severity_norm and in_scope in agreement. Several appear more than once, because distinct findings in the artifact share a class and a line while differing in callee or enclosing method, and nothing is deduplicated (AAP 0.3.2). The three rejected records appear in the dataset not at all, exactly as a counted rejection should.

row_derivations_note: One entry per row, in row order. Each names the fixture member every field was read from, the raw artifact index the record was captured from, the class key the coordinate reduced to, which index scheme resolved it, and either the allowlist glob the path matched or the reason it matched none. file_line_count_at_the_pin is the resolved file's real length in the pinned checkout, which is what makes each start_line checkable rather than merely plausible. The three records that produced no row are under rejections, one entry each.

fields_absent_on_every_row.cwe: A Joern finding names a bytecode call site, not a weakness catalogue entry, and this shape carries no CWE member. Deriving one from a query identifier would be inference.
fields_absent_on_every_row.cve: The same: this shape carries no advisory identifier.
fields_absent_on_every_row.package_coordinate: The same, and the absence is explicitly not a rejection condition here -- unformable_package_coordinate covers a dependency-oriented record, which this is not.

members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.note: Each of these is present in the fixture and must not appear in any row. Checked by substring comparison against every field of every row above, not merely by inspection.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.method: The enclosing method's full signature. Carried into a rejection's identity as diagnosable context, never into a row -- and never into message, however readable it looks.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.file: The frontend's ephemeral extraction path for a .class member. The runner metadata names it record_path_field_to_ignore, and it is never read as a path; reading it as one would relativize a temporary directory into a plausible-looking wrong answer for every row.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.path_resolution: Not present in this fixture at all. Were it present, AAP 0.5.4 confines it to the rejection record and to no dataset field, so it would still reach no row.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.envelope_members: tool_version, cpg, graph, query_set and queries are envelope metadata: not findings, and they produce no rows.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and finding_index name the same record. finding_index is carried as well because normalize.adapters.joern puts exactly that key into the rejection's record_identity, so a produced Rejection and this expectation can be compared directly without translating one coordinate system into the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 pass: the record is a JSON object, it carries the non-empty rule identifier joern-process-exec, and it carries a non-empty message. The only thing left to reject it for is its path.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's reported line of 344 is never examined and non_integer_start_line is not in play.
rejections.why_no_candidate: No source file under src/main or src/test in the pinned tree is named 'NativeLibraryLoader' in the package 'org/sparkproject/io/netty/util/internal', and none declares that type: the class is the shaded Netty native-library loader, vendored into Spark's assembly JARs under the org.sparkproject relocation prefix. It is in the graph because the frontend ran over every JAR the build produced, and a shaded third-party class has no source coordinate in Spark's tree.
rejections.collector_path_consequence: This provisioning's shape carries no path member at all, so the collector fallback branch has nothing to emit and the rejection stands. Had a root-relative path been present, the record would have become a row on that path with the basis already-root-relative and a note that this run's index could not corroborate it.
rejections.collector_explanation_destination: Nothing to place: this shape emits no path_resolution member, so collector_explanation_present stays 0 and no suffix is appended. Where one is present, AAP 0.5.4 confines it to the rejection's detail and to no dataset field, and paths.resolve_bytecode_class composes it on every rejection route.
rejections.expected_detail: no source file under src/main or src/test in the pinned tree is named 'NativeLibraryLoader' in the package 'org/sparkproject/io/netty/util/internal' or declares that type, so the bytecode class 'org.sparkproject.io.netty.util.internal.NativeLibraryLoader' has no source coordinate in the tree
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, quoted here because unresolvable_path covers several routes: naming the class alone would not distinguish a bytecode class no source declares from a uriBaseId chain that cycled. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings -- the simple name, the package and both source trees -- rather than by full-string equality.

expected_record_identity.file: the record's file member, the frontend's ephemeral extraction path for the .class member, carried as context and never read as a path

rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies finding_index and the context members it found -- method, callee and file in this shape -- then the rule identifier once step 2 has passed; the resolver adds coordinate_field, the raw coordinate under the key class, and the reduced class_key. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value. The file member's literal value is an absolute temporary path in the artifact and is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row, so a record whose coordinate resolves to nothing has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or giving it a guessed path -- would each hide it.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The record carries the label of its query, but a rejected record is never fed to the severity tally, so nothing from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this record contributes none.
rejections.contributes_no_path_kind: The record produced no path, so it contributes to no path_kind_* counter and to non_filesystem_paths not at all. It does contribute to rule_id_from_query_id and coordinate_from_class, because it reached those steps before being rejected -- which is why those two counters read 14 against 11 rows.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and finding_index name the same record. finding_index is carried as well because normalize.adapters.joern puts exactly that key into the rejection's record_identity, so a produced Rejection and this expectation can be compared directly without translating one coordinate system into the other.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_UNRESOLVABLE_PATH constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten. Asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another.
rejections.classification_step: step 4 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. Steps 1 to 3 pass: the record is a JSON object, it carries the non-empty rule identifier joern-message-digest, and it carries a non-empty message. The only thing left to reject it for is its path.
rejections.start_line_never_examined: Step 5 is never reached, so this record's reported line of 85 is never examined and non_integer_start_line is not in play.
rejections.why_no_candidate: No source file under src/main or src/test in the pinned tree is named 'MessageDigestHashFunction' in the package 'org/sparkproject/guava/hash', and none declares that type: the class is shaded Guava, vendored under the same relocation prefix. This is the very class reject-joern-unresolvable-path.json reports, so that negative fixture's coordinate is now provably a value the raw artifact carries rather than one chosen to fail. It is in the graph because the frontend ran over every JAR the build produced, and a shaded third-party class has no source coordinate in Spark's tree.
rejections.collector_path_consequence: This provisioning's shape carries no path member at all, so the collector fallback branch has nothing to emit and the rejection stands. Had a root-relative path been present, the record would have become a row on that path with the basis already-root-relative and a note that this run's index could not corroborate it.
rejections.collector_explanation_destination: Nothing to place: this shape emits no path_resolution member, so collector_explanation_present stays 0 and no suffix is appended. Where one is present, AAP 0.5.4 confines it to the rejection's detail and to no dataset field, and paths.resolve_bytecode_class composes it on every rejection route.
rejections.expected_detail: no source file under src/main or src/test in the pinned tree is named 'MessageDigestHashFunction' in the package 'org/sparkproject/guava/hash' or declares that type, so the bytecode class 'org.sparkproject.guava.hash.MessageDigestHashFunction' has no source coordinate in the tree
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, quoted here because unresolvable_path covers several routes: naming the class alone would not distinguish a bytecode class no source declares from a uriBaseId chain that cycled. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by its distinguishing substrings -- the simple name, the package and both source trees -- rather than by full-string equality.

expected_record_identity.file: the record's file member, the frontend's ephemeral extraction path for the .class member, carried as context and never read as a path

rejections.record_identity_note: The adapter supplies finding_index and the context members it found -- method, callee and file in this shape -- then the rule identifier once step 2 has passed; the resolver adds coordinate_field, the raw coordinate under the key class, and the reduced class_key. Enough to find the record in the artifact again, and never the record itself and never a secret value. The file member's literal value is an absolute temporary path in the artifact and is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is no path to put in the row. path is never absent from a row, so a record whose coordinate resolves to nothing has no valid row representation, and the alternatives -- dropping it, or giving it a guessed path -- would each hide it.
